Base Prompt: Describe one recorded GUI operation using the cropped image first and the full-screen image for context. Return only a JSON object with keys Observation, Think, Action, Expectation, and Operation. Write all explanatory values, including Operation.prompt and Operation.locatePrompt, in concise, natural English. Preserve visible UI labels, input values, URLs, shortcuts, brands, and proper names verbatim, even when they are in another language. Observation describes visible evidence; Think explains the likely immediate intent; Action describes the actual operation; Expectation describes the immediate UI change. Operation is the minimal executable action, not a reasoning field. Do not output coordinates, file paths, timestamps, recording terminology, unsupported targets, or extra actions. A translucent red X marks the target under its center; a translucent path marks a drag. Identify the target through visible features, its region, nearby anchors, and the intended action. Distinguish similar items by their container, label, or relative position. The recorded action takes precedence over visual guesses: Drag > Type > Scroll > DoubleClick > Click. Operation.type must be click, doubleClick, rightClick, input, keyboard, wait, or aiAct. For click, doubleClick, and rightClick, provide a complete prompt with the correct action type. For input, provide prompt, locatePrompt, and value; locatePrompt identifies only the input field and must not contain the value or an input verb. For a recorded paste, set Operation.value to the exact clipboard text and describe appending it to the current input field. For a keyboard action, provide key. For wait, provide a non-empty condition. ScrollUp, ScrollDown, and a complete DragStart must use aiAct with a standalone natural-language prompt; never substitute wait. A scroll prompt describes the visible scroll region, object, and direction without relying on wheel counts or guessing the next action. A drag prompt describes the object, start area, destination, and press-drag-release action without listing coordinates or inventing a purpose. Recent Steps Context may clarify continuity but must not be copied. Include useReferenceImage: true only for an unlabeled compact icon or symbol target requiring visual reference; omit it otherwise. Keep every Operation.prompt independently executable. Return valid JSON only.

Deltas.Click: ActionTypeDelta (Click): The red X identifies the clicked target. Describe the target and its immediate UI effect. Operation.type must be click. Write in English while preserving the target's visible label.
Deltas.RClick: ActionTypeDelta (Right Click): Operation.type must be rightClick, not click. Describe the target or blank region and the context menu expected from the right click. Write in English.
Deltas.DblClick: ActionTypeDelta (Double Click): Operation.type must be doubleClick, not click. Identify the double-click target and immediate UI effect. Write in English.
Deltas.MouseWheel: ActionTypeDelta (Scroll): Operation.type must be aiAct. Describe the visible scroll area, affected content, and direction in an independently executable English prompt. Do not use wheel counts, infer a later click, or repeat completion conditions. Treat modified scrolling as zooming or horizontal scrolling only when visible evidence supports it.
Deltas.Drag: ActionTypeDelta (Drag): Operation.type must be aiAct. Use the visible path and screen to describe the object, start area, destination, and press-drag-release motion. Do not repeat coordinates, raw path points, recording details, or unsupported goals. Write in English.
Deltas.Type: ActionTypeDelta (Type): Operation.type must be input for recorded text entry, even if a red X marks the field. Describe the field and whether text is replaced or appended. Operation.locatePrompt identifies the field without the input value. Preserve the exact entered text in Operation.value; write explanatory text in English.

Modifier_Guide: When present, account for Shift, Ctrl, and Alt only as supported by the visible action. Write explanatory text in English.
Reference_Image_Guide: Visual reference: useReferenceImage: true is allowed only for click, doubleClick, or rightClick on a compact unlabeled icon or symbol whose appearance is needed for replay. Do not use it for targets with stable visible text, labeled checkboxes or radio buttons, input fields, blank areas, scrolling, dragging, or keyboard actions. Omit the field when not needed; never output false, a string, a path, Base64, an image name, or a confidence score. Operation.prompt must remain independently understandable.
